scope: Four named Panama legal holds only; operative authority and territorial scope before metadata, streams, EPG or rights.

common_legal_findings.statutory_recognition: Law 72/2008 Articles 13–15 protect coordination/consent and provide for traditional-organization recognition; Law 467/2025 Articles 77–79 recognize binding traditional-justice decisions and necessary resources.
common_legal_findings.classification_rule: First-level or autonomous special-status territorial legislature with substantive binding general norms and budget/executive-control powers; customary authority can qualify without a sovereign or comarca label.
non_inferences: No inference that unwritten customary law is invalid.
No inference that collective land ownership or national-development participation proves parliamentary legislative powers.
No inference that being nested in a district/province or representing few communities defeats autonomy.
No transfer of the separate Emberá-Wounaan comarca Charter to these institutions.
Unavailable governing instruments are not evidence of absence of authority.

sources.title: Law 72 of 23 December 2008, Gazette 26193 (30 December 2008)
sources.read_access_scope: Downloaded complete 9-page Legispan/judiciary PDF; read relevant law text.
sources.finding: Collective title is issued to communities represented by traditional authorities. Articles 13–14 require resource-management coordination and free, prior and informed consent; Article 15 expressly provides executive recognition of traditional organization and authorities. Article 16 finances demarcation. These provisions preserve governance but do not name each congress’s full allocation of powers.

sources.title: ANATI current normative directory: Executive Decree 223 of 29 June 2010
sources.read_access_scope: Search-indexed official directory passage; direct page 403. Decree article text not certified in this pass.
sources.finding: ANATI continues to list the Law 72 implementing decree; a titling-procedure reference is not a congress-level legislative charter.

sources.title: Law 467 of 24 April 2025, Gazette 30265 (25 April 2025)
sources.sections: Title III,Articles 77–79; Article 113; official Gazette page 23
sources.read_access_scope: Read search-indexed official PDF text of Articles 77–79 and 113; opened 33-page PDF is predominantly image text.
sources.finding: Traditional justice in comarcas and collective lands is recognized; traditional-authority decisions must be obeyed unless revoked or annulled by competent authority, with necessary resources guaranteed. This is legally consequential jurisdiction, not a specific assignment of general legislative or budget-approval power to these four congresses.

sources.title: Procuraduría de la Administración: Law 467 legal status
sources.sections: Vigencia 25 April 2025; subrogation of Law 16/2016; Decree 25/2025 and 6 May 2025 erratum links
sources.finding: Use Law 467 rather than the superseded 2016 community-justice law; the noted erratum concerns Article 97, not Articles 77–79.

sources.title: Executive Decree 4 of 20 January 2025, Gazette 30204 (24 January 2025)
sources.sections: Amendment to Decree 203/2018, representation list of 12 traditional organizations
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed official Gazette passage naming all four organizations; full 43 MB Gazette exceeded web reader limit.
sources.finding: All four named bodies are recognized participants in the national development-governance framework. The representation list does not itself allocate broad territorial legislative powers.

sources.title: MinGob-hosted Análisis Sociocultural PN-L 1157, March 2019
sources.read_access_scope: Downloaded full 232-page PDF; extracted/readpp 42–49 and targeted consultation passages. File hosted 2025, substantive report datedMarch 2019.
sources.finding: Describes distinct general, regional and local structures, customary decisions, own Wounaan collective lands plus comarca membership, Alto Bayano communities and Bribri clan consensus. Note 77 contains an apparent Ngäbe-Buglé/Emberá-Wounaan label slip; that sentence is not used as an operative jurisdiction rule.

sources.title: FSC Indigenous Foundation: Continúa el proceso de fortalecimiento de la gobernanza tradicional
sources.sections: Tierras Colectivas Emberá,Wounaan y Eyabida; May 2023 validation and 2022–23 workshops
sources.read_access_scope: Read complete project account, including named authorities and regulation subjects. No regulation text/download or adoption resolution supplied on the page.
sources.finding: A Tuira regional regulation process covered justice, authority/marriage certification, resource rights and restrictions on outsiders. This confirms substantive governance; regional validation is not proof of the General Congress’s complete current governing instrument or financial controls.

sources.title: FSC Indigenous Foundation: Carta Orgánica project account
sources.sections: Sobre el proyecto; Congreso Nacional del Pueblo Wounaan
sources.read_access_scope: Read complete account; Wounaan section identifies a people-wide charter process. Main article concerns Naso, whose 180 articles and validation date are not attributed to Wounaan.
sources.finding: Identifies a distinct Wounaan Charter process and nationwide community representation. It does not publish the adopted Wounaan Charter or certify its operative allocation of powers.

sources.title: COONAPIP territorial workshop report: Tierras Colectivas Emberá-Wounaan
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed PDF passage; direct FCPF  host 403.
sources.finding: Own organizational account distinguishes the General Congress from the comarca and lists five regional congresses. Historical community counts and membership are not treated as current legal boundaries.

sources.title: COONAPIP territorial workshop report: Congreso Nacional Wounaan
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed PDF passages; direct FCPF  host 403.
sources.finding: Separates Wounaan national affiliation from the comarca/collective-lands jurisdiction of some members and identifies its own eastern communities. It records an organization formed 2001; ministry-project accounts elsewhere say 1998, so the founding date is not resolved or used to decide scope.

sources.title: COONAPIP territorial workshop report: Emberá Alto Bayano
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed PDF passage; direct FCPF  host access limited.
sources.finding: Describes the General Congress above local congresses and Council of Nokos, and the communities’ ordinary district/provincial location. This is evidence of the institution’s distinct customary structure, not a finding that nesting extinguishes autonomy.

sources.title: MinGob: Ministro Henríquez firma acuerdo con miembros del Congreso de Alto Bayano
sources.sections: 13 October 2015; agreement signatories and land-title commitments
sources.finding: Identifies the cacique and Congress president as separate agreement signatories for Ipetí and Majé collective-land issues. It supplies no general legislative charter.

sources.title: MinGob: Inicia proceso de consultas con los pueblos indígenas
sources.read_access_scope: Read ministry text naming the three separately represented Emberá congresses.
sources.finding: Comarca, collective-lands and Alto Bayano leaders are separately identified; their powers must not be merged.

sources.title: MinGob/MINSA PMAS: Nuevo Centro de Salud de Puerto Lara
sources.read_access_scope: Read searchable published PDF text including location, grant statement and annex index. The scanned signed land-authorization instrument was not independently transcribed/read. HostedApril 2026 does not redating 2022 consultation.
sources.finding: Places Puerto Lara in the Wounaan Congress’s territory and reports its land-use/administration authorization for MINSA. It does not establish a general legislative/financial constitution.

sources.title: Wounaan authors: Wounaan Storying as Intervention
sources.sections: Project origins; national congress plenary approvals 2017/2019; FUNDEPW distinction
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed original-research passages; indigenous Congress leaders/members are coauthors.
sources.finding: Records national plenary approval for community projects and distinguishes the sibling NGO. Project consent and NGO administration are not automatically a legislative budget or executive-accountability system.

sources.title: MinGob: reunión con autoridades del territorio Bribri
sources.finding: Confirms distinct traditional executive and Council offices and a territorial-governance agenda; does not publish the operative Council rules.

sources.title: ACICAFOC: Bribri community plans adopted 13 July 2025
sources.read_access_scope: Read complete participant account; neither adopted plan text nor detailed maps/budget clauses attached.
sources.finding: El Guabo,Namüwökir,Dakle and Bris approved plans with land-use rules and Council strengthening. Their full normative reach and institutional accountability require the actual plans and governing instrument.

sources.title: Supreme Court Sala Tercera Bribri/ANATI case in Gazette 30597 B,25 August 2026
sources.read_access_scope: Read indexed official passages about 2019/2021 ANATI decisions and coordinate/jurisdiction issues. Individual 21-page PDF opened but text inaccessible; terminal retrieval returnedHTML. Judgment date, full dispositif and all grounds not certified.
sources.finding: A current official litigation lead warns against describing Bribri title/delimitation as settled. It is not used to negate customary authority or decide legislative scope.

records.name: Congreso General Tierras Colectivas Emberá y Wounaan
records.decision_basis: Retain a specific authority evidence hold. The General Congress and local/community decision structures are documented separately from the comarca. The Tuira regulation process covers justice, authority certification, resource rights and outsider restrictions; generic law recognizes collective-land customary justice. The current congress-level allocation of general binding norm-making, financial approval and executive accountability is not established by the instruments obtained; neither eligibility nor an ordinary-local/cultural-only exclusion is justified.
records.territorial_and_institutional_reach: A distinct multi-community General Congress outside the statutory Emberá-Wounaan comarca, with regional congresses documented in its own account. The 2023 Tuira regulation belongs to a regional formation within this network; its scope cannot be silently expanded to all five historical regions or the General Congress.
records.confirmed_legally_consequential_powers: The General Congress and local/community decision structures are documented separately from the comarca. The Tuira regulation process covers justice, authority certification, resource rights and outsider restrictions; generic law recognizes collective-land customary justice.
not_yet_established: Exact current territorial/community membership and jurisdiction of the General Congress versus Tuira and other regions.
Which body may adopt/amend/enforce general rules across the collective-lands network.
General Congress approval/audit of territorial finance and its appointment, removal or supervision of caciques/administration.
remaining_authority_instruments: Current adopted governing statute/Carta Orgánica or authenticated customary-law record of the General Congress, with territorial annex and adoption/amendment record.
Full Reglamento Interno de la Región del Tuira validated in May 2023 and its final adoption/operative record, identifying powers reserved to the General Congress.
The applicable executive recognition/coordination instrument under Law 72 Article 15, if issued, and congress resolutions or customary rules establishing budget and executive controls.
records.currentness_limit: Dated 2026 review with sources of differing dates; no claim that an unobtained charter has not been adopted. No current electoral-activity or exhaustive amendment certificate.

records.name: Congreso Nacional Pueblo Wounaan
records.decision_basis: Retain a specific authority evidence hold. Primary indigenous and government accounts document plenary approvals, its own collective-land communities and a Puerto Lara land-use authorization. Law 467 recognizes consequential traditional justice. Members’ existing comarca jurisdiction and nationwide affiliation overlap; the 2010 account explicitly distinguishes them. The current congress-level allocation of general binding norm-making, financial approval and executive accountability is not established by the instruments obtained; neither eligibility nor an ordinary-local/cultural-only exclusion is justified.
records.territorial_and_institutional_reach: People-wide Wounaan congress with members inside the Emberá-Wounaan comarca and other congress territories, plus its own collective-land communities outside them. This is not simply a third chamber of the comarca, nor merely an NGO: WPNP/CNPW and the sibling FUNDEPW must remain distinct. The name National does not establish a national parliamentary chamber.
records.confirmed_legally_consequential_powers: Primary indigenous and government accounts document plenary approvals, its own collective-land communities and a Puerto Lara land-use authorization. Law 467 recognizes consequential traditional justice. Members’ existing comarca jurisdiction and nationwide affiliation overlap; the 2010 account explicitly distinguishes them.
not_yet_established: Whether the current Wounaan Charter grants the national plenary autonomous territorial general-law powers over specified own lands or primarily coordination/consent alongside local/comarca institutions.
Current adoption, territory, membership and conflict rules of the Charter developed in 2022–23.
Congress budget approval and accountability of the cacique/administration/FUNDEPW; NGO financial personality is not the same grant.

Applicable traditional-organization recognition instrument under Law 72 Article 15, if issued, and rules separating CNPW territorial powers from comarca and other congress powers.
Financial statute and plenary resolutions establishing who approves/audits resources and controls the cacique/executive, with FUNDEPW’s separate role.

Generic law respects traditional authority, but its specific allocation cannot be inferred from a title application or development-plan report. The ministry describes clan-based consensus;2025 participant evidence names El Guabo,Namüwökir,Dakle and Bris. Do not make territorial title or cross-border jurisdiction claims from ethnic continuity.
